name: devilsDeal
source:
You're sitting in your office chair, at your high-powered job. You have three years left, and by god you're going to enjoy them. You pull the packet out of your sport-jacket pocket, gingerly unzip it, and sprinkle some of the contents on the table. You cut it into four lines, and start snorting. You look up after the second line, and it's *him*. 
 
 Your blood runs cold, before the rush hits you. 
 
 `` Enjoying yourself, James? ``, he asks sardonically. 
 
 When you used to picture the devil, he was red-skinned with hooves and a pitchfork, or a suave man in a business suit, perhaps. Not even close. He's an old man with a crooked smile and a bowler hat, with a gaudy ruby ring on his left ring finger. He's leaning forward on a thin black cane with a red handle. 
 
 `` You've done well for yourself, or, I should say, I've done well for you. But, regrettably, something has come up.'' 
 
 He looks at you with a frown. You're sweating profusely, now. Is he taking you early? Fuck. FUCK. 
 
 `` I'm'offering' you a new deal. Your soul back, for one favor.'' 
 
 You're speechless, at first. 
 
 `` W-What do you want, Master? ``, you manage to stammer out, heart pounding from cocaine and terror. 
 
 `` I need you to hire someone. My son.'' 
 
 He hands you a C.V., and you're taken aback. It's blank, except for a name and a picture. You gather your courage. 
 
 `` Is this a joke?'' 
 
 He stares at you with beady eyes. You blink and look away. 
 
 ``... Send him up. ``, you manage. 
 
 He tips his hat and smiles, before disappearing. No noise, or special effect. He's just gone. 
 
 You reach under your desk, hands passing over your gun and finding your bottle of whisky. 
 
 With unsteady hands, you pour yourself a drink.
retelling:
Perspective: The Devil's Son (unnamed)

In the heart of a bustling city, cloaked within the confines of an unassuming high-powered office, I found myself waiting, my eyes fixed on the man seated behind the desk. A seasoned executive, with three years left before retirement, he was known as James. My father, The Devil, had sent me to him.

The atmosphere in this office was thick with tension and the pungent aroma of cocaine. As I stood there, my heart raced. This man held the key to my future. My name, a faceless entity on the CV in his hands, my face staring back at him from its corner, was all that connected me to this world.

From the shadows, The Devil emerged, an old man with a crooked smile and a bowler hat, adorning his head like a sinister crown. A gaudy ruby ring sparkled on his finger, the symbol of my family's power. With a wave of his hand, he startled James out of his stupor.

"James," The Devil began, "We have a deal. But I offer you a new proposition. Your soul in exchange for hiring my son." He gestured towards me, the only clue as to who I was.

I could see the fear and shock in James's eyes, but also something else - curiosity, perhaps. The old man's offer was as intriguing as it was terrifying. And yet, with a swift nod, James agreed. A drink was poured, whisky sloshing against the glass, as he seemed to be coping with this strange turn of events.

For me, this was just the beginning. The deal was sealed, and I was one step closer to entering this world. But what awaited me here, in this office, was a mystery yet to unfold.
